title: Q2 QBR - Summit Retail - Health Check
summary: Quarterly business review focusing on May usage spike, cost drivers, two reliability incidents, roadmap requests for private deployment and improved autoscaling. Action items include pricing for Dedicated, SOC2/security docs, and a targeted performance benchmark scheduled for mid-June.

Roadmap alignment and upcoming feature requests

transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-06-06 Time: 16:00 UTC. Duration: 55 minutes. Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Claire Jensen (Summit Head of ML), Derek Moore (Summit VP Eng), Sana Ali (Summit Data Eng)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, is this still good time?
[00:05] Claire: Yep, this works. We have about an hour.
[00:10] Jordan: Great, we'll do a quick QBR health check—look at usage, costs, reliability, and roadmap asks. Priya will cover health, Mateo on performance and benchmarks.
[00:22] Priya: Cool. Claire, Derek, Sana — thanks for the context in advance. First off, usage summary: your token usage spiked ~42% in May versus April, primarily from the customer support reranker and nightly vector refresh. The cost bump looks like two parts: more tokens and a couple of long-running batch jobs that didn't hit cache.
[00:40] Claire: Yeah we saw that. The vector refresh ran full re-embed for historic tickets — that was on us. But the other big one was live chat. Latency increases caused retries.
[00:52] Mateo: Right, so on the latency/retries: our logs show a couple of incidents May 12 and May 27 where requests fell back to hosted variants because the dedicated pool filled up. There was a routing fallback to smaller model which increased token counts because of re-chats, and also added latency.
[01:10] Derek: Can you explain 'dedicted' pool? We saw references in the console but not sure what triggered fallback.
[01:15] Jordan: Sorry, 'dedicated' — sometimes the transcript says dedicted — but basically Dedicated capacity is your reserved GPU pool. When utilization spikes beyond the autoscale burst threshold, Redwood can route to hosted or a compatible variant. We use policies to avoid surprises, but your current policy is fairly tight which caused the fallback.
[01:33] Sana: Is there a way to prevent that? Our SLOs for chat are 200ms p95.
[01:37] Mateo: A couple of levers: 1) increase reserved capacity (dedicated commit), 2) tune autoscale thresholds and add higher burst capacity, 3) use prefix/KV cache to reduce load for repeated contexts. We saw your KV cache hit rate was low during the refresh window — K V cash in the logs, transcriber spelled it odd — but it's real.
[01:57] Claire: What's the cost delta on increasing committed capacity vs relying on hosted?
[02:02] Jordan: Good question. High-level: dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at steady state; hosted is cheaper for infrequent bursts but can be unpredictable at scale. We'll send a model showing per-token economics with your current traffic shape.
[02:18] Derek: Any security concerns moving more to Dedicated or Private? We have compliance needs — SOC2, data residency for EU customers.
[02:25] Priya: We have SOC2 and ISO docs; Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) supports customer-managed networking and KMS integrations. We'll share the security whitepaper and network diagram. For EU residency we can provision region-specific endpoints.
[02:40] Claire: How hard is Private deployment? Our infra team is cautious about on-prem.
[02:44] Mateo: There are two paths: VPC-hosted private control plane (simpler) or full on-prem package. On-prem needs more ops but gives max isolation. We recommend starting with VPC and testing the autoscaling there.
[02:58] Sana: Regarding the May incidents — any quick wins to avoid similar ones?
[03:02] Mateo: Yes: raise autoscale burst capacity, set a higher threshold before fallback, and implement prefix caching for the support workflow. Also shard the nightly jobs to avoid a single burst. We'll provide specific config suggestions.
[03:18] Claire: We want to schedule a benchmark — particularly 12k qps synthetic to see if Dedicated will hold.
[03:22] Jordan: Mateo can run a targeted benchmark. Mateo, feasible mid-June?
[03:28] Mateo: Yes, I can do 2026-06-20, run your top-5 prompts, include KV-cache on/off and measure p95/p99.
[03:36] Derek: We'll give the prompt list and expected success criteria — accuracy + latency targets.
[03:41] Priya: On cost control, we can also recommend quantization profiles for some models to lower token CPU/GPU cost. We have Redwood Optimize recommendations that helped another retail customer.
[03:55] Claire: We looked at Anthropic/OG providers — any migration concerns?
[03:59] Jordan: There are tradeoffs — model quality, latency, and cost. We support many open models and can do A/B rollouts in the Console. Also, watch out for API differences and tokenization.
[04:12] Sana: Your logs mentioned KV cache eviction rates — is that configurable?
[04:16] Mateo: Yes. Cache TTL and size are tunable per-route. For the support case increase TTL and ensure the prefix matching is stable. That should dramatically cut tokens for repeated contexts.
[04:29] Claire: What about observability — we need per-route cost breakdown for FinOps team.
[04:33] Priya: The Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns per model/route. We can give you an extended retention for the FinOps dashboard as an add-on.
[04:42] Derek: Any blockers on our side to try Dedicated for the support workflow?
[04:46] Jordan: Mainly contract and sizing. We'll put together a dedicated sizing + pricing proposal. Also need confirmation on data residency and KMS.
[04:55] Claire: We accept the sizing exercise. Please include EU region options.
[04:59] Jordan: Noted.
[05:02] Mateo: Quick technical note — during May incidents we saw longer KV lookup latencies in one of your replicas leading to timeouts; asking infra for network config helped. If you can share topology we'll double-check.
[05:15] Sana: I'll share our network diagram after the meeting.
[05:18] Priya: Action items recap: Jordan to send pricing and dedicated capacity proposal by 2026-06-09; Priya to share SOC2/ISO and audit logs docs by 2026-06-08; Mateo to run bench on 2026-06-20; Derek/Claire to share prompts and success criteria by 2026-06-10.
[05:35] Claire: Sounds good. Also please include estimated monthly cost change for both increasing Dedicated commit and alternative autoscale changes.
[05:41] Jordan: We'll include a cost comparison table.
[05:44] Derek: One more ask — can we have a joint runbook for incident response when fallbacks happen?
[05:49] Priya: Yes, we can draft a runbook with steps, who to page, and temporary mitigations.
[05:54] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll share materials and schedule the benchmark. Meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcript has occasional speaker label swaps and minor transcription errors (e.g., "dedicted" for "dedicated", "K V cash" for KV cache). References: pricing spreadsheet (link noted in chat), SOC2 whitepaper (link), network diagram (to be shared by customer).
